title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from the neighbouring pages. k is a field of finite type, typically a number field. S is a curve over k with function field K = k(S), so K/k is a function field in one variable. U → S is a family of hyperbolic curves (the 'U' over S of the next page) with generic fibre U_K. E_K = Gal(K̄/K) is the arithmetic fundamental group of Spec K. E_{U_K} → E_K is the fundamental extension of U_K, with geometric kernel π. A section of U over S, i.e. a K-point of U_K (equation (29) of earlier pages), gives a section of E_{U_K} → E_K. The previous page asked how to relate this section to the family of sections of E_{U_s} over E_{k(s)} at the closed points s, where k(s) is a residue field rather than a subfield of K.

What this page does.
(1) Places as points. For s ≠ generic point, the residue field k(s) is a finite extension of k. Each closed point s determines a conjugacy class of decomposition subgroups Δ_s ⊂ π_K (= E_K). The marginal note recommends replacing S by its complete regular model over k, so that every place of K/k is a point s.
(2) Normalizers. The N_s are precisely the decomposition groups of classical theory, viewed as normalizers. Δ_s is an extension of Gal(k(s)) by the inertia group, so one can consider sections of the map relating E_{k(s)} and E_K. Concretely these are lifts Gal(k(s)) → Δ_s ⊂ E_K, i.e. 'tangential' splittings, and these lifts are permuted under conjugation.
(3) Restriction. Composing such a lift with the given section E_K → E_{U_K} yields a partial section of E_{U_K} over E_{k(s)}, hence an action of Gal(k(s)) on π.
(4) Good reduction and f defined at s. In this case the resulting section is again 'of the first kind': it is the section attached to the rational point f(s) ∈ N_s(k(s)) of the special fibre, via specialization / the comparison π_1(U_{K̄}) ≅ π_1(U_{s̄}).
(5) Otherwise (next page). One obtains an action 'of the second kind', normalizing a cusp inertia subgroup L_i of π, i.e. a cuspidal / tangential section.
(6) Planned next step. The next page proposes to study bad-reduction places, with the modular curve at the cusp ∞ (Tate curve) as the model case.

Overall, the page sets up the 'specialization of sections' along places of a function field: restricting function-field sections to decomposition groups to obtain sections over residue fields. This serves the section conjecture and Grothendieck's distinction between first-kind (rational-point) and second-kind (cuspidal) sections.
errors: Not a mathematical error, but there is a subtlety the page glosses over. k(s) is not a subfield of K. A homomorphism E_{k(s)} → E_K exists only after choosing a splitting of the decomposition group over its residue quotient. Such a splitting exists in the henselian/complete setting (e.g. via a uniformizer / tangential base point), and it is unique only up to inertia conjugation. The page signals this ('sections ... et les conjugués') but does not settle it.
The claim that the specialized section is of first kind needs good reduction of U at s and that the point f extends to s. The 'Attention' remark appears to flag exactly this kind of caveat.

ideas.what: Decomposition groups at closed points of a curve over k, as normalizers, giving conjugacy classes Δ_s in Gal(K)
ideas.modern_name: decomposition/inertia groups of places of a function field

ideas.what: Restricting a section of π_1(U_K) → G_K to a splitting of the decomposition group at s to obtain a section over G_{k(s)}; under good reduction this recovers the section of the specialized point
ideas.modern_name: specialization of sections (section conjecture over function fields vs residue fields)
ideas.usually_credited_to: J. Stix (Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups, LNM 2054, 2013), also Esnault–Wittenberg and Saïdi
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's letter to Faltings (1983) states the section conjecture but not this specialization procedure

ideas.what: Dichotomy between sections of first kind (rational points) and second kind (normalizing a cusp inertia L_i), arising at places where the point does not extend or the reduction is bad
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal / tangential sections; packets of cuspidal sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings), later Nakamura and Stix

missed.claim: Grothendieck plans a systematic study of which kinds of Galois actions on π are obtained by specializing a function-field section at places of bad reduction. His model case is the modular curve at the cusp ∞ (Tate curve). This links the section conjecture over function fields with degeneration and tangential base points.
missed.quote: les sections de l'extension de E_{k(s)} → E_K ... est aussi de première espèce
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Specialization of sections at bad-reduction places is still only partially understood. It is relevant to reducing the section conjecture from function fields to number fields. It was developed later by Stix and Saïdi, and by Nakamura and Ihara for tangential degenerations. This page shows Grothendieck already framing the problem around 1981, though without results.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early unpublished formulation of specializing anabelian sections along decomposition groups, together with the first-kind / second-kind dichotomy. Both are now known from later work (Stix, Nakamura). The page is a sketch with no finished result.
